dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agency personnel involved in foreign assistance, intelligence, and law enforcement coordination, as well as foreign law enforcement agencies.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary of State may establish a program to provide assistance to strengthen the capacity of law enforcement agencies of the countries described in subsection (e)

dimensions.assessment: Provides administrative, technical, and investigative training assistance and reporting requirements focused on transnational crime.
dimensions.evidence: training regarding financial investigations, money laundering and illicit finance prosecution, and asset forfeiture related to PRC-linked transnational criminal organizations

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes a program of assistance and reporting without specifying monetary spending amounts in the text.
Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to add a new program and reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: Chapter 8 of part I of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2291 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following

dimensions.assessment: Establishes an ongoing assistance program and requires a one-time report within one year.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of National Intelligence... shall submit a report

missing_information: Specific funding amounts or budget appropriations for the assistance program.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes a program for U.S. assistance, training, and coordination with law enforcement in Latin America and the Caribbean to address PRC-linked transnational criminal organizations, and requires an interagency report.
